opportunity.title: Jury Management Solution (JMS) System (Presolicitation)
opportunity.agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
opportunity.description: Pre-solicitation notice for a web-based Jury Management System for the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts. The solicitation is unrestricted and not set aside for small business; the Judiciary is not subject to the FAR small business regulations. The AO plans a single-award IDIQ for a commercial off-the-shelf web-based jury management solution that supports selecting, managing and tracking jurors, performs financial and statistical calculations, and interfaces with the Judiciary's financial management system, Momentum. The draft solicitation USCA27R0009 gives requirements and evaluation criteria. The due time is listed as TBD.

supportedClaims.text: The buyer is the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AO) issuing a presolicitation for a Jury Management Solution (JMS) System.
The requirement calls for a single‑award IDIQ contract for a commercial off‑the‑shelf web‑based jury management system that integrates with the Judiciary’s Momentum financial system.
The anticipated IDIQ is expected to have a seven‑year ordering period and an estimated ceiling of $38,000,000.
The system must perform financial and statistical calculations and integrate with the Judiciary’s Momentum financial system.

droppedClaims.text: The procurement has no set‑aside (NONE), making it an unrestricted opportunity open to all businesses.

rationale.point: NAICS 541511 matches company primary NAICS and place of performance (DC/MD/VA) aligns with AO location
Set-aside is NONE (full and open) so SDVOSB certification provides no competitive advantage

Requirement calls for commercial off-the-shelf jury management system with Momentum financial system integration; company past performance is VA software maintenance and Army Guard web portal, not jury management or Momentum integration
$38M ceiling over 7-year IDIQ represents significant scale jump from largest past contract ($3.4M) with 22-person team

risks: No prior relationship with Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
Full and open competition likely attracts large incumbents with existing jury management COTS products
COTS requirement implies need for existing product license/partnership not currently verified
Momentum integration specificity creates technical risk without demonstrated experience
nextSteps: Identify COTS jury management vendors with Momentum integration for potential teaming
Assess whether 22-person team can support IDIQ task order volume at this scale
Request solicitation details to evaluate evaluation criteria and past performance requirements
Determine if Secret clearance and SOC 2 Type II provide differentiation in full and open competition
